correctness.rationale: The probability normalization follows from Cauchy perimeter identity int_0^pi width(K_r,theta)dtheta=L+2pi r. For any fixed polygon and small scaled length rs, compactness and positive edge lengths localize each contributing chord to exactly one vertex wedge. The unit-rounded wedge has arc–arc offset depth H=1-sqrt(1-s²/4) except two symmetric arc–tangent normal strips of width a_s=asin(s/2). In those strips the exact depth is h_m=1-cos(arccos(1-s sin a)-a). Integration J_omega=omega H+Psi and total turning sum omega=2pi yield the invariant m. Independent numerical integration of Psi/s³ for s=.8,.4,.1,.04 converges to -1/30, and exact small-s expansion of H gives pi s²/4 and pi s⁴/64. The finite meshed rounded-polygon verifier is approximation, not proof of exact all-polygon statement.
residual_risks: Small r depends on fixed polygon and s; angular restriction avoids overlapping tangent/fillet strips and must not be extended to all chord lengths.

value.rationale: The result supplies an exact local stochastic-geometric invariant for every polygon: after disk rounding, the normalized first shape-dependent short-chord coefficient recovers the integer vertex count independently of corner-angle distribution. Exact cross-shape universality under fixed perimeter and m is a nontrivial fingerprint a future researcher could use for inverse geometry; it is neither an arbitrary numerical sample nor only a coefficient fit.
